chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Abbas al-Razzaz from Ayoub ibn Nuh, all together, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Baseer al-Asadi and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halbi and Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Divorcing three times in one sitting, if it was upon a state of purity, then it is one (divorce), and if it was not upon purity, then it is nothing.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man divorces his wife three times at once while she is pure?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a single revocable divorce (talaq raj'i) and a nullified pronouncement based on the wife's state of purity (tuhr). It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the timing of the pronouncement relative to the menstrual cycle, ensuring that simultaneous triple divorces are not automatically treated as three separate irrevocable divorces unless specified by context. This ruling underscores the importance of procedural correctness in marital dissolution within the Ja'fari school of thought.
